I am running a structural equation model with an ordinal DV (1 = no, 2 = probably, 3 = yes).
I want to perform a three-way interaction with social origin (4 categories), gender (2 categories) and cultural capital (latent ordinal variable). 
I tried to use indProd(), however, I do not have access to the suggested literature. I've tried many things like:

dat <- indProd(study, var1 = 4, var2 = 11, var3= 15:17, match=F)
dat1 <- indProd(study, var1 = 4, var2 = 12, var3= 15:17, match=F)
dat2 <- indProd(study, var1 = 4, var2 = 13, var3= 15:17, match=F)

and

study <- data.frame(study, predict(model3.fit))
library(dplyr)
study <- study %>%
  
  mutate(cap.female = cultural.capital * female)

messages.subject: Re: Three way interaction with 2 observed and one latent variable
parts: cultural capital (latent ordinal variable).

You mean that it has ordinal indicators?  lavaan does not support categorical latent variables; they are assumed normal.
 
I tried to use indProd()

That assumes indicators are continuous.  Since you have 2 categorical predictors, you could fit an 8-group model (combinations of social origin and gender), test invariance of the latent predictor across those 8 groups, and then place constraints on the latent variable's effect on the DV that are consistent with null hypotheses of no interaction with gender or social origin.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Three way interaction with 2 observed and one latent variable
parts: What I am supposed to do?

Honestly, for such a complex interaction, you are probably better off calculating scale means and using standard regression techniques to check whether there is evidence of your hypothesized three-way interaction on the outcome (or the mediator; the syntax doesn't make it easy to match your variable descriptions to the variable names in your model; perhaps provide a path diagram and more complete information about each (set of) observed variables).
If you can rule out the three-way interaction, that could simply things quite a bit.  Regardless, you can use the boot package to obtain bootstrapped CIs for any (conditional) indirect effects of interest.  The mediation package might be useful too, but I believe it only accommodates moderated mediation involving 2-way interactions (see section 3.2): https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/mediation/vignettes/mediation.pdf

One day in the future, a lot of this should be simplified in lavaan using the Croon's correction:  https://doi.org/10.1080/10705511.2021.1922283
But these methods are still being developed, and although some limited functionality is implemented in lavaan's experimental (still hidden) fsr() function, latent interactions are not yet available in that format (the paper I linked above was just released).

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
